tests.name: Knowledge-observatory docs — starter baseline
tests.description: Baseline for the knowledge-observatory documentation corpus. RANK-CENTRIC by design: the rerank-on vs rerank-off A/B compares two different score REGIMES (rerank-off = RRF-fused; rerank-on = cross-encoder ~0..1), so an absolute expect_min_score band cannot be shared across both arms — the scale-invariant signal is whether the right doc lands within top-K. Positive cases assert expect_within_top_k and leave score bands unset. LIVE A/B RUN 2026-06-05 (graduated KO, 8419 docs): rerank-OFF run ad5d2170-ffed-4472-912a-437f8f96f8d6 (5/7 met, mean_strong_top1=0.622, max_gibberish=0.560); rerank-ON run 39970d88-c9ea-42b7-ad1a-2b31eb06811e (7/7 met, mean_strong_top1=1.000, max_gibberish=0.002). KEY FINDING: all 5 real cases stay within top-K in BOTH arms (rerank changes scores, not rank-centric pass) — consistent with the 22-case recall corpus (rerank buys only +0.046 recall on docs), which is why rerank stays OFF by default. The gibberish cases below were retuned from this run: under the rerank-OFF default, RRF-fused gibberish tops ~0.56 — INDISTINGUISHABLE from the weakest real hits (also ~0.56), so an absolute ceiling cannot separate them rerank-off (that is the cross-encoder's job: rerank-on collapses gibberish to ~0.00). expect_ids (qdrant UUIDs) backfill remains optional polish; the rank-centric assertions do not need them.
